title: Divine Purpose and Human Responsibility
english: It must be said, especially when the perfect has come, that since one confronts face to face with the truth, seeing in part and through a mirror will have ceased, because the seeing of what is most full will have prevailed.

Regarding how this path is assigned, the blessing of Isaac upon Jacob is invoked, from which it begins: 'From the dew of heaven and the heaviness of the earth.' All that existed was given to the redeemed people from Babylon, as God's inheritance.

And since it is said passively that God will inherit all things for the remnant of the people—namely the fruit of the vine, the generations of the earth, and the dew of heaven—both ways it must be invoked, actively and passively.

Actively, it is said thus: Israel is a portion and an inheritance of God, through nothing other than virtues that approached, being chosen and done and seen voluntarily. The same thought holds for: 'Ask of me, and I will give you nations for your inheritance' (Ps 2:8), regarding all men inheriting from the Savior through pious faith and works of virtue.

If 'to inherit' signifies a passion [passive reception] by the falling verb, the understanding will be this: God will inherit all the aforementioned things, giving them in the manner of an inheritance to the remnant of his people, who are those saying according to the prophet Isaiah: 'Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a remnant, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been made like Gomorrah' (Isa 1:9). And with others: 'If the number of the sons of Israel were as the sand by the brim of the sea, the remnant shall be saved' (Isa 17:10). Having received these prophetic voices, the Apostle brings them forward saying thus: 'And in the present time there is a remnant according to the election of grace, not of works, for if it were of works, grace would no longer be grace' (Rom 11:5).

Having made clear what is possible for us regarding the present saying, we set forth the following. Zechariah 8:13: And just as you were a curse among the nations, the house of Judah and the house of Israel, so I will save you and you shall be in blessing.

Be courageous and strengthen your hearts. For the Lord of all says: 'In the way I intended to harm you by provoking your fathers,' says the Lord of all, 'and I did not repent; so I am now set out and intend in these days to do well for Jerusalem and the house of Judah' (Jeremiah 32:19).

To fall into afflictions and curses comes from nothing other than sin and impiety, since blessing is given by God to the righteous because of what they do and think rightly. For humans being self-determining, having free and autonomous choice, they do to themselves either punishments or the bringing of divine promises. Therefore, the way in which they undergo curses is the same way in which they undergo prosperity and blessing.

Immediately, indeed, He says He is the cause of all good for Judah and Israel: 'Since your fathers were impious and lawless, as to provoke me against them, I did not repent, but I brought what was likely for those who provoked to suffer; so now I am set out and intended to save those of Judah and Israel, and I did not repent' (Jeremiah 32:19).
And it is possible to bring forth testimony from these God-breathed writings.

The inhabitants of Nineveh once sinned and were impiously excessive, as the cry of their evil rose to God requiring punishment, as to say to the Provider and Judge of all: 'In three more days, Nineveh shall be overturned' (Jonah 3:4). Having learned this, the guilty ones, following the path of the one who threatened toward repentance, arrived at a state to confess and to do what would undo the preceding evil. Thus, those having changed their minds, the one who had pre-proclaimed the harm against them repented, receiving the cause of blessing; this did not happen regarding the Sodomites, because of the remaining impiety and sins of theirs, even though the merciful God wished to find a starting point for well-doing among them.
For He says: 'The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has filled [heaven], and their sins are exceedingly great. I will indeed go down to see if according to their evil, which has risen to me...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The distinction between knowing and understanding
english: They are completed; but if not, 'that they may know', he is not merely saying: Having been called out by the cry of great sins, I descend along with them so that the great sins might be found being practiced still, being completed by having fallen under the previously proclaimed punishment; but if they were found lying moderately as those who thought impiously and regarding the forbidden works, let him know them as ours, according to it having been written: 'The Lord knew those who were his, and let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from injustice' (2 Tim 2:19).

In this way of thought the vessel of election Paul writes to the Galatians: 'But once you did not know God, you were serving gods which are not gods by nature; but now having known God, rather having been known by God' (Gal 4:9). For he knows those knowing him, not taking the beginning of knowing them, but of examining them as knowing those having been foreknown, in no way regarding the worthless ones still adhering to wickedness when this is happening.

For it is said by the Savior to those remaining in evils until the time of the completion of the world and the manifestation of the judge of all things, of him being made manifest: 'Depart from me, workers of lawlessness; I never knew you' (Matt 7:23), that is, you never had an experience or a participation of me, nor I of you. For if he took to knowing by what is at hand, it would be the same as knowing; how did he know them as being workers of lawlessness?

Therefore, from the double [nature] of knowing and of not being carried along in the God-breathed writings, according to the other thing, the God who knows hearts knows all, both the righteous and the sinners; immediately, therefore, when the one coming 'sits upon the throne of his glory' to 'judge' kings 'living and dead' (Matt 25:31), he will separate the righteous from the sinners, so that he may lead those participating in righteousness and piety into the kingdom in order to inherit it, but the unrighteous and the wicked, not having loved the neighbor as themselves, he will send to punishment, saying: 'Depart, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire, prepared for the devil and his angels' (Matt 25:41). According to the manner

It is not about understanding, as he says to certain people: 'the knower of hidden things' and 'knowing the mind of all'; 'I have known that you have many sins.' Similarly in the Gospel: 'You are those who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts, because that which is in man, when exalted, is an abomination to God' (Luke 6:46).

According to this theory, we must also understand what is continuously stated in the Gospel: 'But Jesus, having known their thoughts' (Mark 2:8), meaning they had happened to be [thinking] something; for they were staying [in thought] craftily and wickedly, thinking that 'the one knowing the mind of all' would remain hidden.

Just as knowing is according to understanding, against which ignorance is opposed, so also it is possible to know and not to know through experience. For if Paul writes about the Savior as 'did not know sin' (referring to the lack of experiential sin), we take the written thing to be equal to: the one not having experienced sin practically or intellectually. Understanding it as much as is in his power and by what kind of choice it is accomplished, and how he has come to it from the world.

This difference also extends to men; for it is said in Ecclesiastes: 'He who keeps the commandment will not know an evil word' (Eccl 7:29), that is, he will not set himself toward an evil word, the evil word being known by knowledge to the one guarding the divine commandment, which is the word of God; for since there is one knowledge of opposites, he who knows the good word also understands its opposite.

The Scripture announces the duality of knowing also concerning Adam, where on one hand it says he understood what the essence of the woman was—for after giving her after the shaping of the Creator, Adam said: 'This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman' (Gen 2:23)—and later, having known her according to the manner of experience; for it is written: 'Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain' (Gen 4:1). And this is brought about for every man living with a wife, in habitual conversation and in divine instruction.
Immediately also concerning the father of the prophet Samuel...

title: The Certainty of Divine Promises
english: It is written: 'And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and he conceived, and she bore Samuel' (1 Sam 1:20). Regarding this, the meaning is said concerning Rebekah: 'She was a virgin, and a man had not known her' (Gen 24:67). And the virgin Mary, the unwedded one, having heard about the conception of a child from the great angel Gabriel, said: 'How can this be to me, since I do not know a man?' (Luke 1:34).

We consider that the present prophecy has not been bypassed in vain; for this has risen to clarity because of the unclearly spoken thus: 'I will come down so that I may see if they are complying according to their cry that is coming; but if not, so that I may know.' For it was necessary to reveal by what meaning it was said by God: 'So that I may know.'

God did not repent, having thought to punish and to expose the insolent upon something, remaining in the judgment against them; but from what source He repented, to see the opportunity in innate goodness.

Not having known [His intent] to bless Judah and Israel, [He waited for] their remaining in the virtue with which they took up [their task] from the exhortation of God and of His law; for it is said in one of the Psalms: 'He will give blessing to the lawgiver' (Ps 112:3), that is, to those guarding His divine law. Equally, it is brought forth in another Psalm, beginning from here: 'Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in His holy place? He who is innocent in hands and pure in heart, who has not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbor. This one shall receive blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his Savior' (Ps 15:4).

For having been said spiritually: 'Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in His holy place?' an answer is given, delineating who is and what kind of person is the one about whom the question is, that [he is] by hands, that is to say, by action, innocent through purity of heart, not at all having taken his soul in vain, or deceitfully swearing to his neighbor, receiving upon these manly deeds both blessing and mercy from God his Savior. In agreement, it is also brought forth in Proverbs: 'Blessing...'

"...for the Lord upon the head of the righteous." The one who has grasped these saving things will not fall away from the promise, being led into the divine promises by the one saying: 'I have set to bless Judah and Israel, and I have not repented' (Zech 8:8). He remains by his grace so as to do well and to lead into eternal salvation those for whom he has not repented, confirming what he promised: even if your fathers provoked him through sin and impiety, and a curse spoke, he did not repent of the threat, nor did he grant you reconciliation from the evil you had through recognition, but therefore both now let your heart be courageous to expect the gifts from me.

For they shall certainly be of my willing and having set to bless you; for it shall be well with you, as you belong to Judah, the one confessing, and to Israel and Jerusalem. 'For wanting to save all men and to come into the knowledge of truth' (1 Tim 2:4), I threaten, I lash those opposing the knowing of the truth of the super-arrogant salvation, subjecting to a little pain those whom I want to improve and to do well. For thus, having been easily benefited, they shall be saved, my having set without regret to save and to do well those whom I have chosen, so that they may be part of and my inheritance.

If we also wish to have God in a propitiatory relation so that he may dispose well toward us, let our intellect, called the heart, be courageous, having made care for excellent works, so that the things of well-being and endless salvation may exist certainly and irrefutably, having been described and having been made manifest from all things, the curse which held on for a little. Therefore be courageous without doubt, expecting what the truthful God promised; for he having said: 'Be courageous' (Zech 13:7), without doubt the hoped-for good things are to be received.

Having sufficiently described the second volume concerning the prophet Zechariah, at which let us rest, beginning the third discourse, 'providing a word in the opening of the mouth' of God, who also enlightened the prophet with the eternal light.
